clue.text: Like a sort of play that could make critic go mad almost

indicators.note: what something could make out of these letters is a new arrangement of them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the phrase go mad is cut off

parts.note: taken as written, before being shortened

explanation.surface: A drama so bad it might drive a reviewer out of their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GO MAD to GOMA; 'could make' shuffles CRITIC with GOMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A play mixing tragedy with comedy is described by this adjective, as in a tragicomedy.

clue.text: Country inn with memorial outside it

indicators.note: the memorial word sits outside, wrapping round the inn word

parts.note: a relic is something kept as a memorial of the past
a pub is an inn

explanation.surface: A rural inn with a war memorial standing outside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like 'rural' with 'inn', but it is the definition: a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a kind of state or nation, such as France or Ireland.

clue.text: Spiritual advice to Moses in warehouse

definitions.meaning: the spiritual song '..., Moses' opens with that command to Moses
in India and East Asia a storage depot is called by this word

explanation.surface: A spiritual instruction delivered to Moses inside a storehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spiritual' is the noun, an African-American religious song, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, from Malay, names a dockside storage building in Asian ports.

clue.text: Heading north over line, I stare

indicators.note: the turned word goes over and around the letter for line
in a down clue, heading north means the word for I is read from the bottom up

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: A traveller going north crosses a border and gazes about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is not part of the definition: it gives EGO, which 'Heading north' turns to OGE, placed 'over' L.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone, usually with open desire.

clue.text: Where you'd presumably find hellish types with old cricketer under a shadow

parts.words: Where you'd presumably find hellish types
parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, so the damned are in Dis
W. G. Grace was the great Victorian cricketer

explanation.surface: Demons and a disgraced old cricketer gathered under a cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and his realm, as in Dante. W. G. Grace was England's most famous Victorian cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under a shadow is out of favour, an idiom for having lost standing.

clue.text: Affected little devil wasn't sincere

parts.note: an imp is a small devil or mischievous child
someone who acted was only pretending

explanation.surface: A little rascal put on an act of feeling hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Impacted is a synonym of influenced, as in 'communities impacted by floods'.

clue.text: Burning paintings maybe outside private room

indicators.note: the paintings word sits outside, wrapping round the room word

parts.note: paintings are an example of art
a den is a private retreat or study

explanation.surface: Paintings stacked outside a private study, perhaps on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means fiery or passionate; its Latin root means blazing.

clue.text: Presidential candidate once sounded a bit wet

indicators.note: sounded points to a word that is said like the candidate's surname

parts.note: Thomas Dewey ran for US president in 1944 and 1948

explanation.surface: A former presidential hopeful came across as rather feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit wet' suggests a weak person in British slang, but it means damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in morning dew, grass is slightly damp.

clue.text: Troublesome person with stick always set about music maker

indicators.note: set about means the whole string of pieces is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a nag is someone who pesters
a rod is a stick
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A nuisance with a stick forever going for a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' looks like 'attack' but turns NAGRODEER round.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium is an example: a keyboard instrument sounding by vibrating reeds.

clue.text: Inventor showing regret when putting off engineers

indicators.note: putting off means shedding the letters for engineers

parts.note: remorse is deep regret
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: An inventor feels regret when engineers are delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Morse invented the telegraph code named after him.

clue.text: Something sweet to stick around lettuce

indicators.note: the word for stick goes around the lettuce word

parts.note: to glue is to stick
cos is a long-leafed lettuce

explanation.surface: A sweet thing made to cling to some salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar, so it is a sweet substance.

clue.text: Without thinking, building home next to an East Anglian city

indicators.note: next to says these pieces are joined side by side

parts.note: in means at home
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, East Anglia

explanation.surface: Building a house beside a fenland city with no thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in the Fens of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting senselessly or foolishly is doing things in a mindless way.

clue.text: Quail a bit when crossing lake

indicators.note: the coin is crossing, lying across the lake letter and so holding it

parts.note: a bit is a small coin
L stands for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone flinches a little while crossing a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quail' looks like a verb, to flinch; it is the American bird, the bobwhite.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin is another name for the North American bobwhite, a type of quail.

clue.text: Understand an old rocker with very little energy at first did nothing

indicators.note: at first places the very and energy letters ahead of the rest

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy, a little of it
to get something is to understand it
an and a are both the indefinite article
a Ted, Teddy boy, was a 1950s rock and roll fan

explanation.surface: An ageing rock fan, low on energy, finally did nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian dress who loved rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To vegetate is to live idly, like a plant, doing nothing.

clue.text: Lass in evil misbehaving?

indicators.note: letters that misbehave will not stay in their order

explanation.surface: A girl who has turned wicked and is acting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicked female is a female villain, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Plea from someone wet and helpless with a certain peck?

parts.words: Plea from someone wet and helpless
parts.note: a soaked helpless person might beg dry me
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A soaked, helpless person begs, getting only a sure kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peck' looks like a kiss, but it is a unit of volume for grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A peck, a quarter of a bushel, is a unit of volume for grain and other solids.

clue.text: Yes, mama is upset with a child stupidly making bloomer

indicators.note: upset means the letters are tipped out of order
stupidly means these letters are arranged in a muddled way

explanation.surface: Mother is upset because her child has stupidly made a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a gaffe but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This aster flowers around Michaelmas, late September, so it is a bloom.

clue.text: Penultimate part of Shakespearean play is beginning to move into vigorous campaigning

parts.note: Shakespeare's plays have five acts, so Act IV comes last but one

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of move

explanation.surface: Act Four of a Shakespeare play starts moving into a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Activism is energetic campaigning for political or social change.

clue.text: Break with trendy element of festival entertainment

parts.note: in means fashionable
the Fringe is the open part of the Edinburgh Festival

explanation.surface: A fashionable act at a festival takes a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Fringe is the open-access arts festival held alongside the official Edinburgh Festival.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a rule is to break or violate it.

clue.text: Surgery as answer to disease that in extremis takes time

parts.note: a cure answers a disease

indicators.note: in extremis takes only the outer letters of that

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Surgery as a cure for disease, which in the worst case takes time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in extremis' looks like 'in dire straits' but picks the ends of 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Curettage is a procedure scraping tissue from a body cavity, a surgical operation.

clue.text: Celebrity children, not one of them accepting the present

indicators.note: the shortened word takes in the word for the present
not means the letters for one of them are removed from children

parts.note: one of the children is a child
now is the present time

explanation.surface: Celebrity children, none of them happy with the gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one of them' removes CHILD, leaving REN; 'Celebrity children' looks like famous kids, but 'Celebrity' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame, and a celebrity enjoys fame.

clue.text: Writer offering brill Old English

parts.note: brill and def are both slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A writer serving up brill, a flatfish, the old English way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brill' looks like the fish but is slang for brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: It's right to check when there's sign of something wrong inside

indicators.note: inside places the cross mark within the word for check

parts.note: to deter is to check or hold back
a cross, X, marks an error

explanation.surface: It is right to check when something seems amiss inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter is Latin for right-hand, used in heraldry for the right side of a shield.

clue.text: Someone terrible following game around in vehicle

indicators.note: following puts the terrible one after the game
around means the game word is turned backwards

parts.note: nim is a game of taking matches from piles
Ivan the Terrible, tsar of Russia

explanation.surface: Someone dreadful chasing a game round in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A minivan is a small van, a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Start to make everybody walk

indicators.note: start to takes the first letter of make

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: An instruction to get everyone walking.
explanation.definitionFit: A mall is a sheltered walk or promenade, like The Mall in London.

clue.text: Number of fashion items in Mary Quant's era

definitions.note: the decade, a plural noun, when the miniskirt designer made her name

parts.note: six is a number
ties are items of fashion worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A count of fashion pieces from Mary Quant's time.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Quant was a London designer who popularised the miniskirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Quant was the defining London designer of that decade.

clue.text: Biscuit containers the wrong way up

indicators.note: in a down clue the wrong way up means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: pans are containers for cooking

explanation.surface: Biscuit tins turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger snap is a crisp biscuit.

clue.text: Part of island in Caribbean captured by the French

indicators.note: captured by means the Caribbean letters sit inside the French article

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)
WI stands for the West Indies

explanation.surface: Part of a Caribbean island seized by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island' suggests the Caribbean; it is the Hebridean island of Lewis and Harris.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis is the northern part of Lewis and Harris in Scotland's Outer Hebrides.

clue.text: First to collect rags, even when chucked?

definitions.text: First to collect rags, even when chucked?

indicators.note: chucked means these letters are thrown about
first to takes the opening letter of collect

explanation.surface: Someone first in line to gather rags, even discarded ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger picks through discarded things, such as rags thrown away.
